'''Malik Monk''' (born February 4, 1998) is an American [[basketball]] player. He played college basketball at the [[Kentucky Wildcats|University of Kentucky]].

==High school career==
[[File:20160330 MCDAAG Malik Monk rising up.jpg|190px|thumb|Right|Monk [[slam dunk|dunking]] the basketball at the [[2016 McDonald's All-American Boys Game]]]]
Monk committed to the University of Kentucky on November 18, 2015.<ref name=MMcommit>{{cite web|url=http://espn.go.com/recruiting/basketball/story/_/id/14161493/no-5-recruit-malik-monk-commits-kentucky-wildcats|title=No. 5 recruit Malik Monk commits to Kentucky|accessdate=2015-11-18|date=2015-11-18|publisher=[[ESPN.com]]}}</ref> 

Monk attended [[Bentonville High School]] in [[Bentonville, Arkansas]]. As a senior, he averaged 28.6 [[points per game]], 4.4 assist per game and 7.6 [[rebounds per game]]. In 2016, Monk played in the [[2016 McDonald's All-American Game]] and [[Jordan Brand Classic]] where he earned Co-MVP honors alongside Kentucky teammate [[De'Aaron Fox]]. Monk played AAU basketball for Wings Elite. He also participated in the [[Nike Global Challenge]] and NBPA Top 100 camp.

On March 11, Malik played his final game in the 7A Championship game scoring 19 points in the 59-49 loss against [[Cabot High School]].

Monk was a consensus five-star prospect, being ranked #9 overall player in the Class of 2016 by the four main recruiting services [[Rivals.com|Rivals]], [[ESPNU Recruiting Insider|ESPN]], [[Scout.com|Scout]], and 247 Sports.<ref name="Fallsignees">{{cite web|url=http://www.ukathletics.com/news/kentucky-men-s-basketball-signs-six-in-fall-signing-11-19-2015|title=Kentucky Men’s Basketball Signs Six in Fall Signing Period|accessdate=2015-11-19|date=2014-11-19|publisher=University of Kentucky}}</ref>

==College career==
[[File:Malik-Monk-2.jpg|150px|thumb|right|upright|Monk in Kentucky's 2016 Blue-White scrimmage]]
On November 18, 2015, Monk tweeted that he would be attending the [[University of Kentucky]], picking Kentucky over Arkansas after a fierce recruiting battle. <ref>{{cite web | url=http://espn.go.com/recruiting/basketball/story/_/id/14161493/no-5-recruit-malik-monk-commits-kentucky-wildcats | title=No. 5 recruit Malik Monk commits to Kentucky | publisher=[[ESPN]] | date=November 18, 2015 | accessdate=June 29, 2016 | author=Borzello, Jeff}}</ref>

On December 17, 2016, Monk set a University of Kentucky freshman scoring record with 47 points in a win over the University of North Carolina.<ref>https://sports.yahoo.com/news/malik-monk-caps-record-setting-night-with-game-winning-3-pointer-005908272.html</ref> Twelve days later, he scored 34 points on 5 for 7 three point shooting in a 99–76 win over [[Ole Miss Rebels men's basketball|Ole Miss]].<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.espn.com/ncb/boxscore?gameId=400910691 | title = Kentucky beats Ole Miss on Monk's 34 points | work = ESPN.com | date = 28 December 2016 | accessdate = 29 December 2016}}</ref> On January 31, 2017 he scored 37 points against [[Georgia Bulldogs men's basketball|Georgia Bulldogs]].<ref>http://www.espn.com/ncb/boxscore?gameId=400910673</ref>  

At the conclusion of his freshman season, Monk announced that he would forgo his final three years of collegiate eligibility and enter the [[2017 NBA Draft]] where he is projected as a first round selection.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/19074339/malik-monk-kentucky-wildcats-declares-nba-draft|title=Malik Monk declares for NBA draft|website=espn.com|author=Jeff Borzello|date=2017-04-04|accessdate=2017-04-04}}</ref>
